result_text:
Template literals now get the same treatment as other string literals when units are compared for duplication. I haven't run a JavaScript example through it. The unit and duplication tests I ran (`*Unit*`, `*Duplic*` in `codeanalyzer`) completed without errors, but I didn't add a test for the template-literal case.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`. It replaces each `` `...` `` with `""` before the other string replacements. That makes `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` identical, including any `${...}` inside. Code outside the literals is untouched, so a difference there still keeps units apart. `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractor` extends this class, so JavaScript is covered.

The replacement works per line, so a template literal that spans several lines isn't masked.

I put the template-literal step ahead of the quote steps so that a literal like `` `it's ${x}` `` isn't mangled by the single-quote rule. The downside is that a double-quoted string containing a backtick is now masked slightly differently, which I think is rare.
